recorded_sources.title: MolmoAct2
recorded_sources.summary_revised: An open robot foundation-model recipe spanning pretraining, mid-training and adaptation. The talk connects visual understanding and physical reasoning to an action expert, and discusses out-of-the-box deployment plus external evaluation.

recorded_sources.title: Semantic Anchoring for Robotic Action Representations
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Examines how action representations can drift away from the semantics of pretrained vision-language models during narrow robot fine-tuning. It proposes separating shared semantic alignment from private physical-execution features.

recorded_sources.title: MEM
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Adds memory at two temporal scales to VLA policies: compressed recent video and recurrent, textual long-term state. The speaker shows how these help with multistep tasks and adapting after past mistakes without keeping all raw frames in context.

recorded_sources.title: PRTS
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Recasts pretraining as learning a representation of progress toward an instruction-specified goal rather than only predicting demonstrated actions. Contrastive reachability objectives are combined with action prediction before downstream behavior-cloning adaptation.

recorded_sources.title: Learning What to Say to Your VLA
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Instead of updating a frozen VLA, learn which language instructions elicit better behavior. The system searches for useful local language sequences, trains a feedback policy from interaction, and gates language interventions when they are likely to help.

recorded_sources.title: When Vision Overrides Language
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Investigates counterfactual VLA failures where familiar visual scenes override the instruction. A benchmark and inference-time guidance compare language-conditioned with unconditioned action predictions to strengthen language following.

recorded_sources.title: ZETA
recorded_sources.summary_revised: A controlled study of cross-embodiment transfer that separates strict zero-shot evaluation from cases where the target robot appeared in pretraining. Results emphasize gripper-local action coordinates, adequate source-robot coverage, and clear disclosure of target exposure.

recorded_sources.title: EmbodiSteer
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Keeps a Cartesian action policy frozen but performs denoising and constraint guidance in the target robot's joint space. This allows a shared policy to account for each robot's collision geometry without abandoning task-space behavior.

recorded_sources.title: Diagnosing Compositional Generalization
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Asks which task combinations must actually appear in training to support new multi-step compositions. The experiments separate coverage gaps, instruction steering failures, and dependencies between subgoals.

recorded_sources.title: Hang Zhao — Organizing Physical AI Across Timescales
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Organizes physical intelligence around the different clocks at which a robot must operate. The keynote compares coded policies, direct model control, orchestration and agentic skill use under a real wall-clock budget, then separates slower task reasoning from motor execution and fast contact response. A high benchmark success rate can hide an impractical inference delay.

recorded_sources.title: π0.7
recorded_sources.summary_revised: A generalist robot policy trained on diverse data with task and quality metadata. The presentation focuses on preserving the value of broad, mixed-quality data, prompting diverse tasks, and evaluating cross-task and cross-embodiment generalization.

recorded_sources.title: Being-H0.5
recorded_sources.summary_revised: A human-centric approach to cross-embodiment pretraining that combines human interaction videos, robot trajectories and visual reasoning data. Shared action slots provide a common representational interface, with mechanisms to specialize behavior for each robot.

recorded_sources.title: RoboTTT
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Scales robot-policy context using test-time training and fast-weight state rather than retaining an ever-growing raw history window. The presentation studies how task-relevant experience can influence behavior across long sequences. This is online internal-state adaptation; it should be distinguished from an autonomous research agent retraining a policy through experiments.

recorded_sources.title: DreamZero
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Turns a pretrained video generator into a world-action policy that predicts future visual dynamics together with robot actions. The talk studies robot-control generalization from video priors, as well as the latency and modeling trade-offs of joint video/action generation.

recorded_sources.title: Mem-World
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Uses a memory-augmented, action-conditioned world model for robot manipulation. The system queries stored multi-view spatial history based on prospective actions, rather than treating all historical visual evidence as equally important.

recorded_sources.title: TEMPO
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Explores whether a compact representation of motion and command history can improve manipulation that depends on timing. Rather than adding a large explicit memory stack, the paper studies lightweight temporal context for reactive policies.

recorded_sources.title: Diversity You Can Actually Measure
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Studies how the diversity of robot training data should be measured, instead of treating raw trajectory count as the only proxy. The presentation connects diversity coverage to generalization across tasks and physical conditions.

recorded_sources.title: MolmoB0T
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Investigates training a generalist manipulation system through simulation and then transferring it to physical robot setups. The discussion focuses on action, perception and benchmark design for evaluating sim-to-real capability.

recorded_sources.title: What Are We Actually Benchmarking in Robot Manipulation?
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Questions whether familiar manipulation benchmarks measure genuine task understanding, spatial generalization and robust behavior or allow easier shortcuts. The presentation calls attention to evaluation design and the interpretation of benchmark scores.

recorded_sources.title: Sharpa
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Sharpa presents a dexterous-manipulation stack built around three complementary paths: more useful demonstrations, turning reference behaviors into executable skills, and reusing interaction experience across embodiments. Its central argument is that hand-motion video alone leaves out contact, force and recovery information required for reliable manipulation. This is a sponsor presentation, not a controlled comparison of all approaches.

recorded_sources.title: Lightwheel
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Lightwheel describes a data-to-simulation-to-deployment workflow: capture human activity, build or calibrate simulated environments, train and evaluate robot policies, then use deployment feedback to improve the loop. The talk emphasizes measuring whether simulated interactions reproduce real physical behavior, rather than assuming visual similarity guarantees useful transfer. Product and performance claims are presented by the company.

recorded_sources.title: Jim Fan — GR00T 2 and Agentic Robotics
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Connects robot foundation-model post-training to a larger agentic execution stack. A slower code- and tool-using orchestrator can supervise real-time robot-control skills; the keynote also describes world-action modeling, training data, simulation infrastructure and skill discovery.

recorded_sources.title: Negar Mehr — Learning to Interact and Coordinate
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Examines how robots must reason about other decision-making agents, not just static scenes. The keynote connects interaction modeling, coordination, learning and evaluation under multi-agent uncertainty.

recorded_sources.title: BitVLA
recorded_sources.summary_revised: BitVLA explores ultra-low-bit vision-language-action models for edge deployment. Its training recipe combines low-bit language/vision alignment, quantization-aware distillation, and robot-policy training, with a specialized runtime for packed weights. The engineering question is how much memory, energy and latency can be saved without losing manipulation performance; the comparisons are speaker-reported.

recorded_sources.title: EagleVLA
recorded_sources.summary_revised: EagleVLA targets onboard real-time control where cloud latency or limited edge compute can make action predictions stale. It combines future-state anticipation with asynchronous inference and scheduling so a robot can react to more recent observations while maintaining coherent motion. The talk evaluates control frequency, observation-action alignment and real-world task execution, not just raw model throughput.

recorded_sources.title: REACT
recorded_sources.summary_revised: REACT addresses a latency-versus-smoothness trade-off in action-chunking policies. Longer chunks produce coherent motion but can become outdated when objects move; shorter chunks react faster but may be jittery. Rolling denoising revises an ongoing action sequence using fresh observations, allowing the controller to respond without discarding all temporal consistency. It is a reactive-control method, not agentic self-improvement.

recorded_sources.title: TARC
recorded_sources.summary_revised: TARC turns the control-update rate into a learned decision. Instead of replanning at a fixed frequency, a policy selects both an action and how long to hold it, subject to an explicit update budget. The talk applies this idea to locomotion and VLA-style control, asking when expensive inference is actually necessary to retain successful feedback control.

recorded_sources.title: Diffusion ReRoll
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Diffusion ReRoll changes how denoising progresses across time in robot sequence prediction. Conventional full-horizon and causal schedules can commit early to a poor motion prefix; partial re-noising keeps earlier and later steps open to revision. The speaker reports stronger sequence behavior on challenging trajectories and argues that the noise schedule itself is a useful temporal inductive bias.

recorded_sources.title: MoRE
recorded_sources.summary_revised: MoRE proposes a mixture-of-motion-experts design for 3D world models spanning different material and actuator dynamics. A router selects among specialized motion experts rather than forcing a single dynamics model to average incompatible regimes. The recorded presentation was interrupted early by technical problems, so this entry describes the stated approach but does not claim verified empirical results.

recorded_sources.title: Targeting World Models to Compromise Robot Learning Pipelines
recorded_sources.summary_revised: This paper studies a security failure mode of robot-learning pipelines that use third-party demonstrations and generative world models. An attacker perturbs seemingly ordinary visual inputs so the world model generates undesirable behavior under an otherwise benign task prompt; training on those generations can contaminate the downstream policy. The result is a warning about data provenance and model-mediated amplification, not an endorsed attack technique.

recorded_sources.title: Chunk-wise Model-based Policy Optimization
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Chunk-wise Model-based Policy Optimization replaces repeated one-step imagined rollouts with a model that predicts a future latent chunk from the current state and a proposed action chunk. The goal is to obtain useful multi-step optimization signals while reducing recursive model error and backpropagation-through-time instability. The talk reports simulation and bipedal-control experiments; numerical comparisons remain speaker-reported.

recorded_sources.title: FedGuide
recorded_sources.summary_revised: FedGuide considers federated reinforcement learning when robot clients have different dynamics, rewards or initial states. Instead of naively averaging policies, it uses diffusion-based prior alignment and a value-based baseline so each client can retain useful specialization while learning from shared information. The evaluation probes return and stability under heterogeneous settings.

recorded_sources.title: Wolfram Burgard — Challenges to Realize Embodied AI
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Argues that robust embodied autonomy requires more than broad learned perception and action: uncertainty, calibrated confidence, task-stage evaluation and failure handling still matter. The keynote relates older probabilistic-robotics ideas to current foundation models and practical deployment requirements. The useful question is whether confidence and recovery remain reliable after the robot leaves familiar conditions.

recorded_sources.title: General Motors
recorded_sources.summary_revised: General Motors describes its autonomy research program across imitation learning, reinforcement learning and vision-language approaches to driving. The presentation connects large-scale driving experience with deployment-grade validation and explains how the company is approaching more automated driver-assistance capability. Announcements and forward-looking product dates are company statements, not independently established outcomes.

recorded_sources.title: BitRobot / RoboColosseum
recorded_sources.summary_revised: BitRobot discusses RoboCap, an egocentric data-collection device, alongside open tooling and RoboColosseum, an effort to run physical robot evaluations across diverse real-world settings. The central argument is that public robotics progress needs a broader and more repeatable supply of real interaction data and external evaluations. Scale and commercial claims are attributed to the sponsor.

recorded_sources.title: Max Insights
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Max Insights presents its infrastructure for collecting human and robot interaction data and connecting that data to robot-learning feedback loops. The talk discusses egocentric capture, translating human experience into robot-relevant training material, and monitoring whether deployed actions meet intended goals. These are company-described capabilities rather than peer-reviewed benchmark conclusions.

recorded_sources.title: Ego2Robot
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Converts egocentric human activity videos into robot-oriented demonstrations by aligning hand actions and visual appearance. The talk evaluates whether synthesized human-to-robot data improves generalization when mixed with robot data for pretraining.

recorded_sources.title: Learning Human Intention
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Transfers intention rather than raw human motion: gaze and hand cues in egocentric video help predict intended subgoals before generating robot actions. The premise is that intention is more portable across embodiments than exact movements.

recorded_sources.title: Residual co-pilot teleoperation
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Learns a low-level contact-control copilot in simulation, using a human surrogate fitted from a small amount of teleoperation data. Human operators retain high-level intent while the copilot improves precision and demonstration quality on difficult insertion tasks.

recorded_sources.title: FlowDAgger
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Adapts frozen diffusion or flow-based robot policies by mapping human corrections back into the policy's latent noise space. A small learnable module can improve a particular task with a handful of interventions while leaving the large foundation policy unchanged.

recorded_sources.title: BiDexGrasp
recorded_sources.summary_revised: BiDexGrasp studies coordinated two-hand grasps for objects whose size and geometry make single-hand grasping impractical. It combines faster grasp-data synthesis with a learned model that explicitly couples the hands and uses object-relative anchors. The presentation reports simulation, cross-platform and physical-grasp evaluations, distinguishing coordination from simply generating two independent grasps.

recorded_sources.title: KP-Grasp
recorded_sources.summary_revised: KPGrasp represents dexterous grasps as 3D hand keypoints instead of directly predicting wrist poses and joint angles. A flow-matching transformer models the conditional keypoint distribution; inverse kinematics then recovers executable robot commands. The design aims to reduce bespoke grasp losses and test-time optimization while scaling across object shapes and partial point-cloud inputs.

recorded_sources.title: WM-Craftnet
recorded_sources.summary_revised: WM-Craftnet combines depth, tactile sensing, proprioception and interaction history in a recurrent world-model representation for dexterous in-hand manipulation. Predicting cleaned geometry and tactile state acts as a training signal even when deployed observations remain noisy. The talk argues that a world model can serve as a reusable state representation for closed-loop contact control, not only a generator of imagined futures.

recorded_sources.title: Sequential Asymmetric Imitation
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Sequential Asymmetric Imitation learns coordinated two-robot behavior without requiring simultaneous teleoperation of both robots. First one robot is trained; then the second is demonstrated alongside that frozen policy, and the first is corrected for the interaction. This exposes each policy to the other robot's real timing and mistakes, improving waiting, yielding and shared-object handling relative to independently trained policies.

recorded_sources.title: Leave It Better Than Found
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Leave It Better Than Found studies sequential collaboration between independently trained robots sharing an environment. A leading robot may achieve its own task yet leave an obstacle that makes the follower's task impossible. The method uses the follower's value estimate, gated by out-of-distribution checks, to guide how the leader leaves the environment, without joint policy training.

recorded_sources.title: RL Token
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Compresses pretrained VLA visual features into a compact RL token and combines that representation with the base policy's suggested action. Online reinforcement learning then improves difficult execution bottlenecks without updating the full VLA.

recorded_sources.title: Flow Policy Gradients / FPO++
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Improves the stability of reinforcement learning for flow-matching robot policies using per-sample and asymmetric trust regions. The talk also contrasts sampling for exploration during training with more deterministic action generation at deployment.

recorded_sources.title: Neuro-symbolic motion prediction
recorded_sources.summary_revised: This neuro-symbolic motion-prediction talk combines neural trajectory forecasts with probabilistic logic encoding context-dependent traffic rules. A learned trust gate decides when rule-based reshaping should influence the predicted trajectories, since road users do not always obey formal rules. The reported gains are concentrated in difficult or unusual cases, highlighting both the value and limits of explicit constraints.

recorded_sources.title: Roberto Martín-Martín — Learning Without Starting Over
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Argues that robotics should optimize learning potential: how much a system can improve from a small amount of new experience. Examples include pretrained action spaces, safe adaptation from video and feedback, experience selection and deliberate data collection.

recorded_sources.title: EgoScale
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Turns diverse human egocentric video into a dexterous pretraining corpus by recovering camera and hand trajectories and mapping them into a shared robot-hand action representation. The presentation examines visual and embodiment gaps before transfer to real dexterous manipulation. Human motion provides broad motor primitives, but video alone does not supply all contact and force information.

recorded_sources.title: OpenDexGrasp
recorded_sources.summary_revised: OpenDexGrasp considers grasps that are suitable for a requested downstream task, not merely physically stable. For example, holding a container securely is insufficient if the grasp blocks the part a robot needs to use. The approach connects open-vocabulary language goals with object contact and grasp generation, asking whether grasp selection can anticipate intended manipulation affordances.

recorded_sources.title: Play2Perfect
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Pretrains general dexterity through exploratory play in simulation, then specializes the acquired skills for precise, long-horizon assembly. The talk connects early manipulation practice with later insertion and threaded assembly while studying which play and training choices support transfer. The demonstrated recipe is simulation-based rather than imitation of human correction demonstrations.

recorded_sources.title: FACTR 2
recorded_sources.summary_revised: FACTR 2 estimates external joint torque on inexpensive robot arms using signals already available from the motors and a model learned from free-space motion. The estimated force signal is then used to train force-aware manipulation policies without adding a dedicated force-torque sensor. This reframes contact sensing as a calibration and representation problem as well as a hardware problem.

recorded_sources.title: PACE
recorded_sources.summary_revised: PACE separates tactile information into distinct temporal roles for precision insertion. Sustained touch indicates the current contact phase, abrupt changes trigger corrections, and prediction of future tactile evolution supplies an auxiliary learning signal. This structure is intended to handle ambiguous visual states during insertion more effectively than treating tactile input as just another concatenated feature.

recorded_sources.title: Disco / distilled search
recorded_sources.summary_revised: DISCO learns long-horizon rearrangement through progressive-widening tree search in GPU-parallel physics simulation. A learned policy proposes continuous actions, a value function guides search, and search outcomes repeatedly update both. The trained policy-value model is then deployed directly without simulator-based search at test time. The presentation reports improved rearrangement and sim-to-real results; those outcomes have not been independently reproduced here.

recorded_sources.title: GRAIL
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Generates human-object interaction videos with a world model, reconstructs usable motion, and converts it into physically valid humanoid training trajectories. It tests how synthetic loco-manipulation data transfers through simulation-trained controllers to physical robots.

recorded_sources.title: SuperMimic
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Uses a learned differentiable world model and analytic gradients to accelerate humanoid motion imitation. The paper emphasizes GPU-efficient policy optimization and the contrast with reinforcement-learning recipes that require much larger computational budgets.

recorded_sources.title: RoboNaldo
recorded_sources.summary_revised: RoboNaldo trains humanoid soccer shooting through a staged reinforcement-learning curriculum built from a reference kicking motion. The curriculum progresses through motion tracking, accurate ball contact and movement toward the ball, while emphasizing balance after impact. It illustrates how task-specific physics and staged training can produce precise, dynamic whole-body skills; it is distinct from RoboTTT.

recorded_sources.title: Google DeepMind / Gemini Robotics 2.5
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Connects Gemini-based embodied reasoning with dexterous robot action models, exploring both stronger physical reasoning in frontier models and broader generality in motor-control models. The talk includes room-scale whole-body control, dexterous manipulation and reasoning-conditioned behavior. The system combines reasoning and execution roles; the industry presentation does not by itself establish autonomous policy learning.

recorded_sources.title: Boston Dynamics / Atlas
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Describes an Atlas factory workflow that requires part sequencing, barcode inspection, transport and exception handling. The architecture uses a reasoning model alongside a whole-body action model so task decisions and dexterous motion have distinct roles. Company demonstrations illustrate the intended system, while sustained reliability and throughput need operational measurements.

recorded_sources.title: Franka
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Franka Robotics introduces its research-platform direction, including force-sensitive manipulation hardware and the controller/software interfaces needed for reproducible experiments. The discussion focuses on the practical research stack around robot arms, not a new single foundation model. Product specifications and ecosystem plans are sponsor-provided information.

recorded_sources.title: DeTac
recorded_sources.summary_revised: DeTac addresses a sensing conflict in vision-based tactile sensors: embedded markers help estimate force but obscure surface texture. A dual-branch model separates marker/force information from appearance, with cross-branch supervision and paired measurements. The talk demonstrates why preserving both tactile geometry and texture matters for downstream perception.

recorded_sources.title: Finger Eye
recorded_sources.summary_revised: FingerEye places complementary cameras inside a fingertip so a dexterous hand can sense both approach and near-contact interaction continuously. The method combines the visual streams with contact-relevant features for manipulation policies. The reported experiments compare wrist-only vision, one-camera sensing and contact-only tactile feedback on precision tasks.

recorded_sources.title: DAVATaR
recorded_sources.summary_revised: DAVATaR studies manipulation across the air-water interface, where refraction degrades vision and submerged electronics complicate tactile sensing. It combines depth-aware visual augmentation with pressure-transmitting fingertip sensing that keeps sensitive electronics above the water. The work treats underwater contact as a joint perception-and-hardware problem.

recorded_sources.title: Visible Touch
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Visible Touch makes tactile measurements accessible to visual robot policies by drawing contact cues directly on camera images. A low-cost magnetic sensor produces spatial overlays that can be consumed by existing VLA architectures without redesigning their encoders. The reported results suggest that input representation can matter as much as adding new network components for contact-rich manipulation.

recorded_sources.title: Demystifying When and Why VLAs Fail in Contact-Rich Tasks
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Diagnoses two contact-rich VLA bottlenecks: generating precise small actions and responding to temporally structured force information. The presentation changes the post-training noise schedule and introduces short-history, contact-gated force conditioning. These mechanisms target execution and feedback deficiencies rather than visual recognition alone.

recorded_sources.title: Never Too Late for Force
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Never Too Late for Force adds reactive force information to a pretrained visual action policy at post-training time. A force-aware expert can correct actions within a predicted chunk while the base model retains broad visual knowledge. The design asks whether sparse force data can improve contact responsiveness without sacrificing the generalization achieved through visual pretraining.

recorded_sources.title: Constraint-Decomposed Impedance Control
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Constraint-Decomposed Impedance Control infers motion directions consistent with an articulated object's kinematic constraints from samples of a generative policy. It assigns higher stiffness along feasible directions and more compliance in directions likely to create unwanted forces. The approach uses the policy's own trajectory distribution to guide contact-safe execution without requiring a manually specified constraint model for every object.

recorded_sources.title: TAM
recorded_sources.summary_revised: TAM is a small torque-adaptation module that compensates for differences between nominal robot dynamics and actual payload, friction or hardware. It uses recent motion history to adjust torque commands, and can be trained in simulation using randomized free-space interactions. The talk tests this adapter across control policies without fully retraining each underlying policy for a new robot.

recorded_sources.title: Combining Constrained Sampling and RL
recorded_sources.summary_revised: This paper separates the exploration problem in manipulation reinforcement learning from the policy-optimization problem. It constructs a physically constrained state-sampling distribution using contact and feasibility knowledge, so the learner encounters useful modes of interaction more frequently. The hypothesis is that better structured starting conditions can outperform prolonged exploration from arbitrary states.

recorded_sources.title: Physics-Guided Residual Dynamics
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Physics-Guided Residual Dynamics combines an approximate physics simulator with a learned correction for deformable-object motion. Surface particles and velocities estimated from RGB-D observations are simulated using physics, then a residual network adjusts the prediction. Rope and brush-like objects illustrate why neither unconstrained learning nor a hand-tuned physics model is always sufficient on its own.

recorded_sources.title: WireCraft
recorded_sources.summary_revised: WireCraft provides a shared simulation benchmark for industrial deformable-linear-object tasks, including connector insertion, routing through clips and seating in channels. It varies geometry and fixtures to make algorithms comparable under consistent evaluation. The talk also discusses mixed simulated and real demonstrations for transferring contact-sensitive wire manipulation to physical robots.

recorded_sources.title: Cloth simulator-in-the-loop
recorded_sources.summary_revised: This cloth-manipulation method uses a simulator as a forward model during inference. A learned reconstruction maps an observed cloth image to a deformable mesh; parallel simulated rollouts then refine a candidate action sequence, and the robot executes the first action before replanning. Unlike a purely reactive policy, it explicitly spends test-time computation to evaluate physical consequences.

recorded_sources.title: Robustness without Wrinkles
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Robustness without Wrinkles develops differentiable deformable-object simulation and robust model-predictive control. Smooth approximations make optimization through contact dynamics tractable; parallel simulation and feedback control account for uncertainty during manipulation. It illustrates the alternative to end-to-end behavior cloning when one can afford physics-based planning at runtime.

recorded_sources.title: NICE — Noise-Invariant Spatial Encoding for 3D Manipulation Policies under Depth Corruption
recorded_sources.summary_revised: NICE trains spatial features that remain useful when depth measurements are unreliable, especially for transparent or reflective objects. Cross-view geometry supervision and uncertainty-aware feature aggregation seek to avoid brittle reliance on corrupted depth pixels. Physical grasping examples examine whether the learned representation transfers to conditions where conventional 3D policies struggle.

recorded_sources.title: Spatial-temporal feature map mobile manipulation
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Conditions mobile manipulation on an accumulated spatiotemporal environment and robot feature map. Explicit spatial history helps a policy handle tasks that extend beyond one tabletop view or one immediate action. The central deployment concern is whether that map remains accurate when the robot revisits places or objects change.

recorded_sources.title: Articulated 3D Scene Graphs
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Articulated 3D Scene Graphs uses observed object interactions to estimate how doors, drawers and other articulated objects can move. The system builds a semantic and kinematic scene graph from RGB-D observations, then uses that structure to execute language-specified mobile manipulation tasks. It combines object identity with executable articulation knowledge rather than relying on a static scene map.

recorded_sources.title: RAM reachability
recorded_sources.summary_revised: RAM predicts whether a robot morphology can reach a requested 3D pose, without solving full inverse kinematics each time. A morphology encoder conditions a learned reachability representation trained on many robot geometries. This supports faster workspace queries and gradient-based morphology optimization when the question is feasibility, not an explicit joint configuration.

recorded_sources.title: Shape Your Body
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Shape Your Body jointly considers learned locomotion capability and robot hardware design. After training a generalist controller and critic across varied morphologies, the system uses gradients through the frozen value function to improve embodiment parameters. It proposes an efficient alternative to repeatedly retraining a separate controller for each candidate robot design.

recorded_sources.title: Russ Tedrake — Learning in the Factories
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Connects industrial deployment with robot learning through work-site experience, measured reliability and intervention-driven feedback. The keynote discusses factory workflows, task economics and how failures can become useful subsequent training data. Success in a controlled workflow and transfer to an unfamiliar setting remain separate evidence requirements.

recorded_sources.title: Meta Robotics Studio
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Describes Meta Robotics Studio’s goal of a home humanoid that is both useful and comfortable to live with. The industry presentation connects autonomous household work with safety, interaction and the larger model-and-system stack required for a home robot. These are team-described goals and capabilities rather than an independently validated general-purpose robot result.

recorded_sources.title: AGIBOT
recorded_sources.summary_revised: AGIBOT describes its physical-AI ecosystem spanning deployed robots, data collection, model development and evaluation. The presentation introduces an open robot-trajectory dataset and argues that standardized benchmarks and fleet experience can direct subsequent training. Deployment and scale figures are company-reported claims rather than independently verified research outcomes.

recorded_sources.title: Tesla
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Tesla describes how it uses learned world models and counterfactual simulation to test robustness under unusual driving and robotics scenarios. The presentation emphasizes predicting the consequences of events that may be rare or unsafe to stage physically, then checking how learned policies respond. The speaker explicitly says the talk does not provide detailed new Optimus-policy results; product claims are attributable to Tesla.

recorded_sources.title: Fei-Fei Li — Atlas World Model
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Presents Atlas, a unified world model for visually consistent generation and reconstruction, with controllable viewpoints and sparse-image conditioning. Robotics motivation includes representation and simulation, but the talk does not establish Atlas itself as a general robot-control policy.

recorded_sources.title: Fei-Fei Li and Lisa Su — Fireside Chat
recorded_sources.summary_revised: A discussion of robotics, world models, hardware/software co-design, frontier models and public research infrastructure. The speakers distinguish the compute needs of large-scale training from the latency, cost and power constraints at robot deployment.

recorded_sources.title: Commercially Viable Generalist Robots — Special Debate
recorded_sources.summary_revised: An explicit debate about whether large-scale behavior cloning and in-domain improvement are enough for commercially useful generalist robots. Arguments cover how to define generality, the economic cost of physical data, real-world reliability, simulation, hierarchy and inference-time computation. Debate sides were assigned by the moderator and should not be treated as fixed personal positions.

recorded_sources.title: Closing and Awards
recorded_sources.summary_revised: Archives the paper awards and conference closing, with separate navigation back to the earlier musical interlude. The award discussion highlights SuperMimic, Play2Perfect, GRAIL, RoboTTT, What Are We Actually Benchmarking and Disco as finalists, and reports RoboTTT and SuperMimic as the student-paper and conference-paper winners. Those announcements are source context, not independent validation of every technical claim.
